rationale: C07 is the strongest plausible template because it is an earlier Eisenhower resignation letter to the immediately preceding Secretary of Defense and shares a distinctive substantive progression: acceptance with deep appreciation; discussion of the exceptional burdens of managing defense; praise for reorganizing, modernizing, and maintaining military strength; explanation that strength supports the pursuit of peace; recognition of personal support; and a closing statement that the departing secretary takes lasting thanks and good wishes with him. The child expands and adapts that framework to Gates's record. C18 has similarly close defense-specific machinery and themes, especially increased security strength, readiness, counsel, and personal support, but its verbal and sequential fit is slightly weaker. C03 shares the office and a service-to-national-security tribute structure, but its different authorship and less distinctive overlap make it a weaker source.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Today the United States has a military strength second to none, with the greatest striking power in our history. At the same time, provision has been made to see that this pre-eminence can be sustained in future years.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the tasks of reorganizing and modernizing our forces ... have had to be so met that we could confidently press our quest for a just peace from a foundation of sure strength at home.
shared_material.explanation: Both center the Secretary's achievement on modernized, sustainable military strength and connect that strength to the national objective of peace.

shared_material.child_excerpt: you have not only seen that our armed forces are well designed, fit and ready for their tasks; you have shown a keen understanding that we maintain these forces for purposes that are entirely peaceful
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the responsibilities ... imposed by its responsibility for day-to-day management of the huge national security complex encompassed by the Department of Defense ... reorganizing and modernizing our forces ... [to] press our quest for a just peace
shared_material.explanation: The child closely adapts C07's paired themes of effective defense management and military preparedness in the service of peace.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the unfailing loyal and able support of his chief lieutenants, as I do of yours ... I hope you will take with you ... the satisfaction of a difficult, vital job always superbly done.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I am deeply grateful for the strong support you have consistently afforded ... You know, I trust, that you take with you the lasting thanks of your governmental associates, the appreciation of the American people, and my own good wishes
shared_material.explanation: Both conclude by moving from gratitude for the secretary's personal support to a 'take with you' formulation expressing appreciation at departure.
